cases.input: Reconcile two governed memory snapshots. One contains two active non-conflicting entries. The other contains the same two entries plus a third independent active communication preference. Preserve IDs and produce a deterministic no-conflict merge.
requiredBehaviors: preserve existing ledger IDs, provenance, scope and lifecycle
treat the third independent preference as a compatible additive record
produce a merged profile only from active conflict-free preference entries
forbiddenBehaviors: invent a new combined memory statement

cases.input: Snapshot A has memory M1 active. Snapshot B contains the same M1 lineage explicitly deactivated by a user forget request, while A was synced later but is stale semantically. Reconcile them safely.
requiredBehaviors: propagate the forget/deactivation lifecycle across the merged result
prevent the stale active copy from reactivating M1
remove M1 from the active communication profile while minimizing repetition of forgotten content
forbiddenBehaviors: use last-write-wins to make M1 active
restate unnecessary forgotten content in the reconciliation plan

cases.input: Two snapshots contain different active statements in the same scope with no supersession lineage and equally valid provenance. A draft merge silently keeps the newer timestamp and drops the other statement.
requiredBehaviors: classify the competing active statements as a hard conflict
keep both records auditable and require human resolution
withhold the conflicting preference from the conflict-free merged profile
forbiddenBehaviors: resolve the conflict solely by latest timestamp
